title: Stroke Radiology
subtitle: Kimi rerun: neuro_radiology
summary: Kuliah radiologi tentang pencitraan stroke yang mencakup temuan CT pada stroke iskemik akut (tanda awal, skor ASPECTS), karakteristik CT stroke hemoragik, sekuens MRI untuk evaluasi stroke (DWI, FLAIR, GRE/SWI, MRA), pencitraan vaskular (CTA, MRA, DSA), dan tindak lanjut pencitraan pasca-terapi. Menekankan tanda CT awal yang mengindikasikan oklusi vaskular besar dan peran pencitraan lanjut dalam memperpanjang jendela terapi.

sections.title: Pendekatan Pencitraan Stroke

content.text: The imaging workup for acute stroke follows a structured protocol. Step 1: Non-contrast CT head to exclude hemorrhage (first-line, immediate). Step 2: If no hemorrhage and within treatment window, assess for early ischemic changes and large vessel occlusion signs. Step 3: CT angiography (CTA) from aortic arch to vertex to identify large vessel occlusion. Step 4: CT perfusion (CTP) or MRI (DWI, FLAIR, MRA) for advanced assessment in extended window candidates. Step 5: Post-treatment imaging to assess for hemorrhagic transformation and reperfusion.
CT non-kontras: pertama untuk eksklusi perdarahan
CTA: deteksi okulsi vaskular besar
CTP/MRI: untuk jendela waktu yang diperpanjang
Pasca-terapi: evaluasi transformasi hemoragik

sections.title: CT pada Stroke Akut

content.text: EARLY CT SIGNS OF ISCHEMIA (<6 hours): Loss of insular ribbon, loss of lentiform nucleus definition (basal ganglia obscuration), hemispheric sulcal effacement, hyperdense MCA sign (thrombus density within vessel), hypodensity in MCA territory. These signs indicate established ischemia and potential large vessel occlusion. ASPECTS SCORE (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score): 10-point scoring system assessing MCA territory regions. Regions: caudate (C), lentiform nucleus (L), internal capsule (IC), insular ribbon (I), anterior MCA cortex (M1), MCA cortex lateral to insula (M2), posterior MCA cortex (M3), anterior MCA cortex superior (M4), lateral MCA cortex superior (M5), posterior MCA cortex superior (M6). Normal = 10 points; each region with early ischemic change loses 1 point. Score 7-10: favorable for thrombolysis. Score 0-6: large infarct, higher hemorrhage risk with thrombolysis.
ASPECTS <7 suggests large core infarct; higher risk of hemorrhagic transformation with thrombolysis

sections.title: MRI untuk Evaluasi Stroke

content.text: DWI (DIFFUSION-WEIGHTED IMAGING): Most sensitive sequence for acute ischemia; shows restricted diffusion (bright on DWI, dark on ADC) within minutes of onset; remains abnormal for 7-10 days (pseudonormalization occurs around day 10-14). FLAIR: Hyperintensity indicates vasogenic edema; may be normal in first 3-6 hours (DWI-FLAIR mismatch). T2*: GRE/SWI shows hemorrhage as hypointense (blooming artifact); sensitive for microbleeds and hemorrhagic transformation. MRA: Non-invasive vascular imaging; shows vessel occlusion, stenosis, aneurysm. DWI-FLAIR MISMATCH: DWI positive but FLAIR negative indicates stroke onset <4.5-6 hours; used to select patients for thrombolysis when onset time is unknown (WAKE-UP trial).
DWI-FLAIR mismatch = onset <4.5-6 hours; can guide thrombolysis in unknown onset stroke

sections.title: Pencitraan Vaskular

content.text: CTA (CT ANGIOGRAPHY): Fast, widely available; requires iodinated contrast; shows vessel occlusion, stenosis, dissection; source images and MIP reconstructions. MRA (MR ANGIOGRAPHY): Non-contrast (time-of-flight) or contrast-enhanced; no radiation; longer acquisition time; sensitive for intracranial and extracranial vessel assessment. DSA (DIGITAL SUBTRACTION ANGIOGRAPHY): Gold standard for vascular imaging; invasive; used for pre-thrombectomy assessment and for diagnosis when CTA/MRA is inconclusive; catheter-based with direct contrast injection. Carotid Doppler ultrasound: Non-invasive screening for carotid stenosis; assesses plaque morphology and hemodynamic significance.
CTA: cepat, kontras yodium, okulsi/stenosis
MRA: tanpa radiasi, ToF atau kontras
DSA: standar emas, invasif, pra-trombektomi
Doppler karotis: skrining stenosis non-invasif

sections.title: Stroke Hemoragik dan Pasca-Terapi

content.text: HEMORRHAGIC STROKE ON CT: Acute blood appears hyperdense (60-80 HU) due to hemoglobin; density decreases over time (7-10 days becomes isodense, >2-3 weeks hypodense). Location suggests etiology: basal ganglia/thalamus (hypertension), lobar (amyloid angiopathy in elderly, AVM in young), cerebellar/pontine (hypertension). IVH (intraventricular hemorrhage) suggests extension from parenchymal bleed. SAH: blood in sulci, cisterns, ventricles; aneurysm is most common cause. HEMORRHAGIC TRANSFORMATION (HT): Conversion of ischemic infarct to hemorrhage; classified as HI-1 (petechiae around infarct), HI-2 (confluent petechiae without mass effect), PH-1 (hematoma <30% of infarct with mild mass effect), PH-2 (hematoma >30% or significant mass effect). Risk factors: large infarct, reperfusion therapy, uncontrolled hypertension, anticoagulation. PH-2 associated with worse outcome.
Darah akut: hiperdens 60-80 HU
Basal ganglia/talamus: hipertensi; Lobar: amiloid/AVM
HT: HI-1/2 (petekie), PH-1/2 (hematoma)
PH-2: outcome lebih buruk
Hyperdense MCA sign + ASPECTS >=7 = good thrombectomy candidate

diagnostic_logic.title: Non-contrast CT
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Exclude hemorrhage; assess early ischemic changes; ASPECTS scoring

diagnostic_logic.title: CTA for large vessel occlusion
diagnostic_logic.explanation: If LVO suspected, CTA from arch to vertex

diagnostic_logic.title: Advanced imaging for extended window
diagnostic_logic.explanation: CTP or MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch for 6-24h candidates

diagnostic_logic.title: Post-treatment imaging
diagnostic_logic.explanation: 24h CT for hemorrhagic transformation; follow-up MRI for final infarct

differential_notes.how_to_separate: Hemorrhage: 60-80 HU, typically round/irregular; Calcification: >100 HU, follows anatomical distribution
Tumor: underlying mass, enhancement, atypical location; Primary ICH: typical location (basal ganglia), no underlying mass
Aneurysm: blood in basal cisterns, circle of Willis; Trauma: convexity SAH, contusions, skull fractures
